documents.unit: Office of the Provost (Academic Integrity), per Faculty Council recommendation
documents.title: Faculty Guidance - Academic Integrity (Academic integrity and AI)
tiers: AI not allowed: all submitted work must be original, no AI writing any part
AI allowed with attribution: permitted on certain assignments, with citation and full text appendix
documents.summary: The Provost academic-integrity faculty page carries a Faculty Council recommendation (October 2023) that every syllabus contain one of two AI statements. One bans AI authorship; the other permits AI on named assignments if cited with the full transcript attached. The rest of the page is a general integrity reporting procedure, not tied to AI.
documents.stance_why: The page recommends that "all syllabi include one of two statements" (not allowed, or allowed with attribution) and leaves the choice to each instructor, so it sets no stance of its own and offers two templates.

units.why: The page says the Faculty Council "has recommended that all syllabi include" a statement, which is a rule on instructors about communicating AI expectations (P09), addressed to instructors at course start.
units.anchor: has recommended that all syllabi include one of two statements
units.frag_end: statements concerning the use or restriction of AI tools in the course
units.fit_note: A recommendation, not a mandate, and the syllabus must pick one of two prepared statements.

units.why: The recommendation offers exactly two statements, "not allowed" and "allowed with attribution", which is a named two-way set of AI-use categories (P05) rather than one default; P04 does not fit as well because the options are named and scripted.
units.anchor: one of two statements concerning the use or restriction of AI tools
units.policy: The recommended syllabus statements come in two named options: AI not allowed, or AI allowed with attribution.

units.why: The reference to "Faculty Council Minutes for Monday, October 2, 2023" says when and by which body the recommendation was made, so it describes how the policy came about (P84).
units.anchor: Faculty Council Minutes for Monday, October 2, 2023, pp. 6-7

units.why: The no-AI statement says students "should not have another person or entity write any portion of an assignment, including ... using AI tools like ChatGPT", which bans having AI produce submitted work (P19) for students during assignments.
units.anchor: should not have another person or entity write any portion of an assignment
units.frag_end: including hiring others or using AI tools like ChatGPT

units.why: The no-AI statement requires that "all submitted work must be original and created by the student(s) alone or in groups", which is ownership of submitted work (P29), a different rule from the specific AI ban.
units.anchor: all submitted work must be original and created by the student(s) alone or in groups
units.frag_start: In this class, all submitted work

units.why: The no-AI statement tells students "If unsure about a source's appropriateness, consult the instructor", i.e. ask before relying on a source (P10).
units.anchor: If unsure about a source's appropriateness, consult the instructor
units.fit_note: Framed around sources generally, not explicitly AI.

units.why: The allow statement says "Use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is permitted in this course on certain assignments", so permission is assignment by assignment (P04) rather than a blanket default.
units.anchor: is permitted in this course on certain assignments
units.frag_start: Use of AI tools, including ChatGPT,

units.why: The bracketed note says "Faculty must either detail the assignments or types of assignments here or clarify how students will know which ones", a duty on instructors to state in the syllabus which work allows AI (P09).
units.anchor: Faculty must either detail the assignments or types of assignments here
units.frag_end: how students will know which ones

units.why: "students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work" is a requirement to acknowledge AI use in the submission (P24).
units.anchor: students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work

units.why: "detailed citations of AI-generated content" asks for more than a bare mention, but does not say which details; P25 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: This includes detailed citations of AI-generated content
units.fit_note: Says citations must be detailed but names no required elements (tool, prompt, date).

units.why: Students must add "the full text of cited ChatGPT (or other Large Language Model (LLM) generator) as an appendix", which is submitting the AI transcript (P26).
units.anchor: adding the full text of cited ChatGPT (or other Large Language Model (LLM) generator)
units.frag_end: generator) as an appendix to the assignment

units.why: "Misuse or failure to cite AI help is considered academic dishonesty" makes nondisclosure itself a violation (P28); it also classifies misuse as misconduct (P36), but the sentence is mainly about citation, so P28.
units.anchor: Misuse or failure to cite AI help is considered academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: Also classifies any AI misuse as academic dishonesty (P36).

units.why: "Ensure AI-generated information is accurate" tells students to check AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Ensure AI-generated information is accurate

units.why: "Contact the instructor if in doubt about using a source" is the ask-first rule (P10) in the allowed-with-attribution statement.
units.anchor: Contact the instructor if in doubt about using a source
units.fit_note: Framed around sources generally, not explicitly AI.

units.why: The page points faculty to a UC San Diego resource "to learn how to craft a policy that addresses AI and GenAI", which supports instructors in learning how to set policy (P63).
units.anchor: use the resource below to learn how to craft a policy that addresses AI

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Guidance
documents.summary: The Center for Learning Design page sets no course rule: faculty choose, with two sample syllabus texts. It describes how instructors and students can use the licensed Copilot Chat, advises authentic assessment, and gives data-protection, detector and access notes.
documents.stance_why: It says "Faculty determine their own policy for generative AI use in their course" and gives two sample syllabus texts (prohibiting AI-based cheating, ethical use), so it hands the decision to instructors with templates.

units.why: "Faculty determine their own policy for generative AI use in their course" puts the decision with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Faculty determine their own policy for generative AI use in their course

units.why: The sample text says AI use for cheating "is strictly prohibited in this course", a ban stated as a default for the course (P01), but limited to cheating purposes, so only a partial fit.
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited in this course
units.frag_start: The use of AI or any other
units.fit_note: The ban covers use of AI or automated systems for cheating purposes, not every AI use.

units.why: The sample text lists "generating papers, presentations, or any other assignments" as banned, i.e. having AI produce submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: the use of AI tools for generating papers, presentations, or any other assignments
units.frag_start: This includes the use of AI tools

units.why: "Any such use will be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy" classifies the banned use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: violation of the academic integrity policy and appropriate action will be taken
units.frag_start: Any such use will be considered

units.why: "Students are expected to use AI tools and resources ethically and responsibly" is a general conduct expectation that fits no existing type exactly.
units.anchor: Students are expected to use AI tools and resources ethically and responsibly
units.uncovered_note: General expectation that students use AI ethically and responsibly, with no specific content.

units.why: "any data used in AI systems is properly licensed" is about legal rights to inputs, matching copyright and licensing (P52).
units.anchor: any data used in AI systems is properly licensed

units.why: "any AI-generated content is appropriately cited" asks for acknowledgement of AI content (P24).
units.anchor: any AI-generated content is appropriately cited

units.why: AI content "shared with others should be clearly labeled as such to avoid misrepresentation"; closest is disclosure (P24), but it covers any shared content, not just submissions.
units.anchor: any AI-generated content that is shared with others should be clearly labeled
units.frag_start: any AI-generated content that is shared
units.fit_note: Labeling applies to AI content shared with anyone, not only course submissions.

units.why: "Any violations of ethical use policies will be taken seriously and appropriate action will be taken" states that misuse is handled as a violation (P36) without naming penalties.
units.anchor: Any violations of ethical use policies will be taken seriously
units.fit_note: Names no integrity process or penalty.

units.why: The intro says AI platforms "can assist instructors in creating customized content ... providing personalized feedback, and assessing student progress", naming benefits for teaching (P87).
units.anchor: AI-powered platforms can assist instructors in creating customized content for courses

units.why: Instructors "can use it to generate content, such as discussion prompts, quizzes, and assignments", an instructor use of AI for teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: generate content, such as discussion prompts, quizzes, and assignments
units.frag_start: Instructors can use it to generate

units.why: Instructors may use Copilot "to evaluate student work and generate feedback" which they should personalize; this is AI-assisted feedback under a condition (P101).
units.anchor: evaluate student work and generate feedback on assignments, essays, and other projects
units.frag_start: Instructors can use it to evaluate
units.fit_note: The condition is that instructors personalize the feedback before giving it; no review process is described.

units.why: Copilot "can help teachers locate and share relevant resources", another instructor teaching use (P59).
units.anchor: It can help teachers locate and share relevant resources
units.frag_end: enhance the learning experience for students

units.why: Instructors may prompt Copilot "to explore potential research topics for themselves or student deliverables", a teaching-work use (P59).
units.anchor: to explore potential research topics for themselves or student deliverables

units.why: "It's important to further research all information collected by a generative AI tool to ensure accuracy" tells instructors to verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: further research all information collected by a generative AI tool to ensure accuracy

units.why: Students can use Copilot "as a tutor or learning partner", i.e. AI as tutor for understanding the material (P12).
units.anchor: using the tool as a tutor or learning partner
units.frag_end: as a tutor or learning partner

units.why: Students can use it to "develop their ideas, structure their arguments, and identify relevant sources", which is writing support (P91); it sits beside the prohibition on generated papers in the sample text.
units.anchor: helping them develop their ideas, structure their arguments, and identify relevant sources
units.frag_start: Students can use it to generate
units.fit_note: Described as generating content for deliverables, which is broader than editing or outlining.

units.why: Students are told "It's important to further research any information collected ... to ensure accuracy" (P31).
units.anchor: further research any information collected by a generative AI tool to ensure accuracy
units.frag_start: It’s important to further research any

units.why: Students can use it "to receive feedback on their work", which is revising own writing with AI help (P91).
units.anchor: use it to receive feedback on their work
units.frag_start: Students can use it to receive
units.frag_end: areas of strength and areas for improvement
units.fit_note: Feedback on work generally, not limited to editing or proofreading.

units.why: Students can use it "to generate study guides or flashcards, or to practice answering sample questions", matching study aids (P14).
units.anchor: generate study guides or flashcards, or to practice answering sample questions
units.frag_start: they can use it to generate study

units.why: "Assessing application, not just recall" is advice to redesign assessments around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Assessing application, not just recall
units.fit_note: Offered as an option; the page does not say instructors must do it.

units.why: "Focusing on process, not just product" is an assessment redesign idea to resist copying from AI (P35).
units.anchor: Focusing on process, not just product
units.frag_start: Focusing on process, not just product
units.fit_note: Offered as an option; not a requirement.

units.why: "Incorporating student choice and creativity" lets students pick topics so answers are harder to copy from AI (P35).
units.anchor: Incorporating student choice and creativity
units.fit_note: Offered as an option; not a requirement.

units.why: The page warns that tools "learn from the material they are exposed to from the users", a fact about data use that supports privacy caution (P50).
units.anchor: Generative AI language tools learn from the material they are exposed to

units.why: "we recommend that you ... not provide the AI tool with materials unpublished or proprietary educational materials" advises against uploading course materials (P49); it addresses instructors and students, and is a recommendation.
units.anchor: not provide the AI tool with materials unpublished or proprietary educational materials
units.frag_start: We recommend that you use these tools
units.fit_note: Recommendation addressed to instructors and students, about unpublished or proprietary materials.

units.why: "students and instructors should read the platform's privacy policy" is advice to protect data and understand tool terms (P50).
units.anchor: students and instructors should read the platform's privacy policy

units.why: "Students and instructors should be cautious about sharing novel ideas, personal, or professional data" is advice to protect personal data (P50).
units.anchor: should be cautious about sharing novel ideas, personal, or professional data
units.frag_start: Students and instructors should be cautious

units.why: "The university has licensed Microsoft Copilot Chat" names the institution-wide AI tool available to faculty and students (P92).
units.anchor: The university has licensed

units.why: Free accounts "are limited in availability based on traffic and capacity, with preference given to paid users", a note on unequal access to AI tools (P51).
units.anchor: limited in availability based on traffic and capacity, with preference given to paid users
units.fit_note: States a fact about access; it does not say anything is optional or provided free.

units.why: "these tools are not always accurate when it comes to distinguishing human-written from AI-generated content" says detectors are unreliable (P39).
units.anchor: these tools are not always accurate when it comes to distinguishing human-written from AI-generated content
units.frag_start: these tools are not always accurate
units.fit_note: Names GPTZero as available and does not say detectors must not be used.

units.why: "always apply critical thinking, check the source, and if possible, verify information through multiple channels" tells instructors how to weigh evidence of authenticity (P69).
units.anchor: always apply critical thinking, check the source, and if possible, verify information
units.frag_start: If you're concerned about the authenticity

units.why: Naming "GPTZero" among free detectors for faculty concerned about authenticity points to detection tools (P40).
units.anchor: There are a number of free tools available, including GPTZero
units.frag_start: There are a number of free

units.why: Entering a paper on "a commonly discussed topic" in Copilot "is okay" gives a data-protection permission with a limit on sensitive work (P50).
units.anchor: entering it in Microsoft Copilot Chat or another Generative AI product is okay
units.frag_start: If the paper or work is about

units.why: Copilot "can support your work by helping you draft and refine course communications, summarize articles ... and generate outlines for syllabi" is an instructor use for teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: helping you draft and refine course communications, summarize articles, reports, or meeting notes
units.frag_start: Copilot Chat can support your work

units.why: The page offers "Book a consult" and "Get Help from Learning Design Services", support for faculty learning AI (P63).

notes: Topic slugs follow the vocabulary used in other coder A files (no AGENT_BRIEF.md found). The Provost page's generic integrity-reporting steps (ten-day notice, Maxient report, appeal panel) are not tied to AI in the text and were not coded. Course layer was deferred in the collect file.
